title: One-to-Many Relations
description: Implement 1:N relations in Prisma, query child collections with filtering, and configure cascade deletions.

data.text: A **1-to-Many (1:N) relation** is the most common relational pattern. One record in the parent table links to zero, one, or multiple records in a child table (e.g., one `Author` has many `Books`, one `User` has many `Orders`).

data.title: 1-to-Many Schema Definition with Index
data.content: Note the @@index on customerId to ensure high-performance lookups.
data.code:
model Customer {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  name      String
  email     String   @unique
  orders    Order[]  // 1 Customer -> Many Orders
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
}

model Order {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
  totalAmount Decimal  @db.Decimal(10, 2)
  status      String   @default("PENDING")
  customerId  String   @map("customer_id")
  customer    Customer @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)

  @@index([customerId]) // CRITICAL: Always index the foreign key!
}

data.title: Advanced 1:N Querying with Relation Filters
data.content: Use `some`, `every`, or `none` to filter parent records based on child attributes.

data.title: Avoid Loading Huge Lists: Use `_count`
data.text: If you only need to show the badge number of orders or comments, use `_count: { select: { orders: true } }` instead of fetching thousands of records over the wire.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The foreign key lives on the 'many' side of the relation.
Always create an `@@index` on the foreign key column.
Use `some`, `every`, and `none` relation filters to query parents based on child criteria.
Use `_count` to fetch relation counts with optimal performance.
